summary: Kern County Fire Department lookout on Midway Peak near Fellows, planned 1939 and finished about 1940 (register says circa 1945); now gone except for a concrete slab.

facts.design: Register: 3 stories (engine shed, living quarters, glass observation room). 1940 reports: wooden building with one downstairs room and garage plus a glass-enclosed second floor
facts.status_note: Completely gone except for a concrete slab, per a peakbagging photo page; register gives removal date as unknown

visit.trail_note: 1940 reports describe a road to the summit, graded over about 4 miles; one report calls it open to the general public and a later one says it is not. No source describes access today.

events.note: Lookout planned on Midway Peak as a PWA project (Bakersfield Californian, May 5, 1939)
Bakersfield Californian reports from July 31 and September 6, 1940: station nearly complete in July and standing on the peak by September; register's circa 1945 date conflicts
Reports differ: one person stationed in summer months; a licensed radio operator on duty about six months a year
Road to the summit completed with WPA labor (Bakersfield Californian, April 6, 1940), described as open to the general public; a July 31, 1940 report says it was not
Register gives construction circa 1945 according to the Thornton survey

corrections.proposed: remove; no source gives a tower height
corrections.why: 182.9 m is 600 ft and no source gives that figure. The register gives an elevation of 3,665 ft for the peak, and the 1940 reports describe a 20 x 20 ft base and a 14 x 14 ft lookout room, with no height. Elevation is already recorded separately as 1117.1 m.

Two Bakersfield Californian reports from July 31 and September 6, 1940, quoted on Forest Lookouts, describe the station as nearly complete that summer and standing on the peak by September. The register's circa 1945 comes from a Thornton survey and may reflect a later date or an estimate. Editor to decide.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says circa 1945 (Thornton survey); 1939 and 1940 newspaper reports describe a planned, then completed, station. The story reports both dates.

Register describes three stories with an engine shed on the ground floor; 1940 reports describe one room downstairs with a garage and a glass-enclosed second floor. The story says the accounts do not match.

Forest Lookouts and peakbagging list the site under San Luis Obispo County; the register says Kern County and the Kern County Fire Department administered it. The 1940 reports place it southwest of Fellows and 14 miles northwest of Taft, both in Kern. Record keeps Kern.
One 1940 report says one person was stationed in the summer months; a later one says a radio operator was on duty about six months a year.
Register gives 3,665 ft; peakbagging gives 3662 ft; a 1940 report gives 3600-foot. Record's 1,117 m is kept from the register.

notes_for_editor: Fate rests on one undated peakbagging photo page ('completely gone except for a concrete slab'); no source describes the site today or its access. Brief status 'gone' is supported by that page; access left unset. Build date: register circa 1945 conflicts with 1939-40 newspapers via Forest Lookouts; correction proposed to 1940, editor to decide. Brief height_m 182.9 (600 ft) has no source; correction proposes removal. Forest Lookouts and peakbagging list the site under San Luis Obispo County, which conflicts with the register's Kern County; the 1940 text places it near Fellows and Taft, so the record stays Kern. Photos: the FFLOS page credits a circa 1945 image to peakbagging.com and peakbagging credits a 6 Sept 1940 newspaper photo, but no image URLs or licences were captured, so none added. Two search calls and four page reads used.
